sources.authors: Pete Bonasso; David Kortenkamp; Carroll Thronesbery
sources.title: Intelligent Control of a Water-Recovery System: Three Years in the Trenches

implemented: Three abstraction levels coordinating deliberation and reactive behavior, reported on several robot platforms; authors report around-the-clock autonomous software operation for 16 months on NASA's Integrated Water-Recovery System test system.
learned: Neither consulted abstract establishes persistent skill acquisition or autonomous goal learning; not classified as a learning demonstration.
designed: Control architecture, compatible description languages, domain-specific skills, operational objectives and integration software.
limit: 16 months is an author-reported operating period, not verified uninterrupted uptime, self-maintenance, a flight deployment, or independently acquired cognition. Detailed failure logs, intervention history and operational criteria remain unreviewed.
ora: A longevity comparator: continuing to execute under designed supervision is distinguishable from maintaining an organism's own substrate or acquiring new competence.

sources.title: A capacity theory of comprehension: individual differences in working memory
The organization of thinking: what functional brain imaging reveals about the neuroarchitecture of complex cognition
sources.access: NLM metadata and indexed abstract via Mendeley; DOI redirect failed

sources.title: The capacity theory of sentence comprehension: critique of Just and Carpenter (1992)
sources.kind: independent published critique, not experimental reproduction

implemented: A production-system model of comprehension with finite activation; later 4CAPS models distributed capacity-limited processing centers and compares selected tasks to behavior and neuroimaging.
learned: Dynamic allocation of modeled activation is reported; these reviewed records do not establish autonomous acquisition of the architecture or its underlying objectives.
designed: Production rules, center structure, capacity constraints and task models.
limit: The working-memory account is contested: Waters and Caplan question the supporting data and explanatory scope and propose an alternative. Model-to-human fit is not a unique identification of biological mechanism. Full quantitative analyses not audited.
ora: Distinguish resource accounting, short-lived allocation and persistent acquisition. A computational budget is not itself metabolism or evidence of cognition.

sources.title: Learning in a hierarchical control system: 4D/RCS in the DARPA LAGR program
sources.access: NIST submitted manuscript, introduction, behavior-generation excerpt, discussion/conclusions and acknowledgements; PDF pages 1 and 32 visually checked; publisher DOI verified; not full audit
sources.programme: DARPA Learning Applied to Ground Vehicles (LAGR); NIST team; external government evaluation team reported; exact contract identifier not established

implemented: Hierarchical control with distributed sensory, world-model and behavior processes. The 2002 author reports only lower levels fully implemented. In the LAGR publication, the team reports learning terrain models and retaining maps and routes between runs; independent government test administration is described.
learned: Experience-dependent changes to estimates, remembered maps and route information in a specified navigation domain.
designed: Hierarchy, sensing, labels/feedback, learning algorithms, cost representation, route objectives, data retention and externally supplied test goals.
limit: Map alignment remains unresolved; some proposed weight adaptation is prospective. Government-conducted tests reported by the authors are not independently reproduced results. Reference design and higher-level ambitions do not establish complete implementation. Exact award number and independent evaluation report not located in this batch.
ora: Separate learned state from authored storage/feedback, and test causal attribution rather than inferring it from competent behavior. Research comparator only; not an implementation recommendation.

sources.title: Embodying a Cognitive Model in a Mobile Robot
sources.access: author PDF text: abstract and introduction; first-page screenshot timed out; DOI indexed separately

implemented: Three component theories had been tested separately by 2004; integration was underway. By 2006 the authors report implementing Robot Schemas within Soar, with robot implementation/testing continuing.
learned: Schema learning described as enabled by Soar; no quantified independent acquisition or generalization result audited in these records.
designed: Concurrent schema language, activation mechanism, Soar infrastructure, representation reformulation and embodied interfaces.
limit: Do not treat the 2004 integration plan or 2006 architectural rationale as a completed full cognitive system. Relationship to previously profiled Soar is explicit, not independent evidence for general intelligence.
ora: A methodological comparator for separating changes in representation from changes in behavior. Trace the origin of representational primitives.

sources.access: one-page primary video-program description and funding text; screenshot timed out; author initial rendered Ian in extraction vs Jan on AAAI HTML

funding.recipient: Guardian project, Stanford University / affiliated medical researchers (formal award recipient not verified)
funding.verification: explicit acknowledgement in indexed primary text; visual authentication and official award record pending

implemented: Architecture that selects reasoning/control methods as context and resources change; Guardian prototype demonstration uses simulated patient progression, with development on simulated and recorded patient data.
learned: No autonomous acquisition of domain knowledge or lasting skill demonstrated by the reviewed description; the knowledge acquisition process is not established as autonomous.
designed: BB1 blackboard controller, domain ontology and knowledge bases, available reasoning methods and data filters.
limit: Laboratory/video example is not clinical deployment or evidence of diagnostic efficacy. Resource-dependent selection among existing methods need not imply durable learning. Funding acknowledgement is text verified only.
ora: Historical comparator for context-sensitive scheduling and selection of existing methods without evidence of newly acquired underlying capabilities.
